# Binary isolation of the radial obstruction at an exact global budget

Use the planar core A,D,B and constants from
`candidate 92e51a4b18979d56`:

    Gamma=4/9, w=103/200, W=13/20,
    M_core=42/25, B_cap=6811/8910.

For every n>=2 there is a full-dimensional convex body in R^n times R^2
with an inclusion-minimal finite cap cover, every cap of the same mass
B_cap, whose exact maximal normalized depth is

    beta_n=Gamma/[2^n-4978/4865] > Gamma/2^n.              (1)

Its ratio to Gamma/2^n tends to one as n tends to infinity. Nevertheless
all sufficiently small independent radial changes of its actual fibers
that preserve convex compatibility, do not decrease total mixed mass,
and do not increase these selected cap budgets are trivial.

There are h=2^n-1 essential cap groups, each of three caps. This is
within the proposed h<=2^n allowance. No duplication is used to call
the count exactly 2^n, and no claim about a minimal cover with exactly
2^n groups is made. The selected groups cover the entire mixed source;
they are not claimed to cover the entire ambient space after isolation.

## 1. An exact lattice-complete base polytope

Write the integer base as (z,b), with b in R^(n-1). Let

    Q={0<=b_i<=1, 0<=z, z+b_i<=2 for every i}.

Equivalently, Q is the convex hull of (0,b) for all binary b,
(1,b) for all nonzero binary b, and (2,0). To verify the upper roof,
for any b in the cube average the binary vectors 1_(u<=b_i) over
0<=u<=1. Their zero-vector mass is 1-max_i b_i. Assign height two
to that vector and height one to the others, obtaining upper height
2-max_i b_i. Lower height zero is the ordinary cube face.

Consequently the exact integer points of Q are

    (0,0),(1,0),(2,0),
    (0,b),(1,b) for nonzero binary b.                   (2)

There are 2^n+1 such points. The only nonvertex point is (1,0),
the midpoint of the core edge. Put the fibers A,D,B at the three
core bases (0,0),(1,0),(2,0). At every other point of (2) put

    rho K,  rho^2=6811/1980<4,

where K is the centered standard triangle. Its area is
rho^2/2=B_cap/Gamma.

Take the convex hull of all these lifted fibers. A section at an
integer binary b can involve only generators at that same b, since
each coordinate is an extreme coordinate of [0,1]. At b=0 the
only nontrivial midpoint requirement is D=(A+B)/2, so the three
core traces are exact. At any other binary b, the two z endpoints
are exposed and there is no integer z between them. This proves
all actual integer fibers are precisely the specified ones. The
hull is full dimensional in R^(n+2).

## 2. Explicit finite isolation and the cover

Use the canonical continuous normals

    l_0(x)=-x_1-x_2, l_1(x)=x_1, l_2(x)=x_2.

All original supports in these directions are strictly below two:
they equal 2/3 on each core fiber, and 2rho/3<4/3 on a regular
fiber. The core group consists of

    l_i(x)>=2 sum_j b_j,  i=0,1,2.                     (3)

It captures no mass in any noncore fiber and restricts on the core
to the original through-zero cover. Each cap has mass B_cap.

For each nonzero binary vector v define the affine function

    delta_v(b)=sum_(v_i=0)b_i+sum_(v_i=1)(1-b_i).

For p=(0,v) put ell_p=2delta_v(b)+z; for p=(1,v) put
ell_p=2delta_v(b)+1-z. On the lattice set (2), ell_p vanishes
exactly at p and is at least one at every other point. The group
assigned to this exposed fiber is

    l_i(x)>=2 ell_p(z,b),  i=0,1,2.                    (4)

These caps capture only their own fiber, on which each has exactly
Gamma times its area, namely B_cap. Their union covers that entire
fiber because l_0+l_1+l_2=0. The core group covers its three fibers.
Thus (3)-(4) cover the actual mixed source, with all budgets equal.

Every individual cap is essential. At a regular fiber, its associated
simplex vertex has positive own margin and negative margins for the
other two caps. All other groups exclude this fiber strictly. At the
middle core fiber use the corresponding vertex of K contained in D;
again the other groups strictly exclude it. Hence there is no redundant
cap in this displayed finite cover.

## 3. Exact global maximum and comparison with the target

The cover proves the absolute depth of every source point is at most
B_cap. At the centroid of any exposed regular simplex, retaining its
own fiber already gives absolute depth at least B_cap by ordinary
simplex depth. Hence the global absolute maximum is exactly B_cap.
The total mass is

    M_n=M_core+(2^n-2)B_cap/Gamma.

Since Gamma M_core/B_cap=4752/4865, this gives (1). In particular

    beta_n/(Gamma/2^n)=2^n/[2^n-4978/4865] -> 1.

This certifies the actual maximal depth, rather than only a cap-cover
upper bound. The core caps have the globally critical numerical budget;
it is not asserted that each core cap passes through a global maximizer
on the core. The exposed regular centers suffice for exact maximality.

## 4. No nearby radial escape even when every fiber may change

Scale each fiber about zero by a positive factor differing from one
by less than 1/10, while keeping all caps (3)-(4) fixed. Their isolation
is preserved: every continuous support stays below 22/15<2. Thus
each regular cap still has mass exactly B_cap times the square of
its own scale. Cap nonincrease forces every regular scale to be
at most one, so their aggregate mass does not increase.

If total mixed mass does not decrease, the three core fibers must
therefore have total mass at least M_core. Their selected cap budgets
are still the original core budgets because all other fibers are
excluded. Actual convex compatibility still imposes
(r_-A+r_+B)/2 subset r_0 D. The independently audited finite core
obstruction now forces all three core scales to equal one. Total
mass nondecrease then forces every regular scale to equal one as
well. This proves the claimed full-array radial obstruction.

General nonradial changes, moving cap normals, moving the common
centroid section, or selecting another cap cover are outside this
statement. The values in (1) are strictly above the desired bound.
No counterexample to that bound or any unrestricted variational
classification is claimed.
